newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels kill 30 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill 30 in Algeria.

text.p: Moslem rebels slaughtered 30 people, including two babies and seven women, overnight at Chebli village in Blida province 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, Algerian security officials said on Thursday.
The massacre, the second in the area in just over a month, took place hours before the start of a three-week campaign for June 5 parliamentary elections.
People who visited the area shortly after the massacre to enquire about relatives said Moslem rebels stormed the remote farm community, shooting to death or slashing the throats of 30 villagers.
"They arrived at about midnight. They were about 50 armed men," said one resident quoting a survivor. Another resident, speaking by telephone, said the victims lived at a remote collective farm.

"The survivors are still under the shock of the killing. Many have begun gathering up their belongings to leave for safer areas," he said. He reported survivors said rebels doused two bleeding women with fuel and set them on fire.
Algerian security forces, in a six-line statement, said the 30 people were "assassinated in a cowardly way" -- the term used by authorities when Moslem rebels cut the throats of their victims.
Among the 30 victims were 17 children, two babies and seven women, they added in the statement reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.
In the last attack in Chebli, guerrillas cut the throats and hacked to death 30 people on April 13, according to the authorities.
The killing came just before the start of campaigning in the first parliamentary election in five years, which authorities promised would usher in an era of stability.
About 60,000 people have died in strife between Moslem guerrillas and government forces since 1992, when authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
